items.title: Mrs. Francis Oliver Interview, 1969-05-10
items.q: Yes, it is for the Mouton. Because I never have dropped my father's name.

ctx.x: Well. I had it off there for a while. But your grandmother's name— Excuse me, I just don't use the breakdown. No, that's all right. I understand. I certainly understand. Your grandmother's name then was Mimi, too. No, my great-grandmother's name was Mimi, yes. But your name then really was Mimi named after her. Yes, I am. Mimi Francis was your— That's right. But you dropped the Mimi.

Well, I don't—you know, I put Francis M. Oliver all the time. And the M's can either be for Mimi or Mouton. That's what I thought it was for the Mouton. Yes, it is for the Mouton. Because I never have dropped my father's name. Yes.
How come that the—Gellarrow changed—he evidently took that name then. He took it—he named it—
